summary: On Windows the atomic exchange is the one mutation in the whole type that is performed by absolute path rather than relative to the retained no-follow parent handle: it rebuilds paths from the `_parentPath` string captured at Open() and calls ReplaceFileW, which re-resolves every ancestor component and both operands with normal reparse-point following and is subject to MAX_PATH.
failure_scenario: Every other mutation (OpenChild:1239 with FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT, RenameWindowsHandle:1562 with FILE_RENAME_INFO.RootDirectory = ParentHandle, CompareUnlink:857 with FileDispositionInfoEx on the handle) is anchored to the retained directory handle and cannot be redirected. ExchangeRetainingPrevious drops that anchor: an attacker who converts any ancestor of _parentPath into a directory junction between Open() and the ReplaceFileW call redirects the publication, and ReplaceFileW additionally transplants the *replaced* file's DACL onto the replacement (only recovered because ApplyOwnerOnlyAndVerify runs afterwards at Store:701/1586). Separately and non-adversarially: with an installation path longer than MAX_PATH and long paths not enabled, first publication (handle-relative, no limit) succeeds while every subsequent revision fails Unavailable at Store:618 — a silently one-shot journal.
verifier_reason: Primitives.cs:593-594 builds `MapWindowsReplaceFileArguments(_parentPath, journalLeaf, workingLeaf, previousLeaf)` from the captured path string and :596-597 hands it to ReplaceFileW, and the contrast is exact: OpenWindowsChild:1239 passes `FileNonDirectoryFile | FileOpenReparsePoint | FileSynchronousIoNonAlert` at :1293, RenameWindowsHandle:1562 writes ParentHandle into FILE_RENAME_INFO.RootDirectory at buffer offset 8, CompareUnlink:857 sets the disposition on the handle itself — and ExchangeRetainingPrevious is indeed the only mutation lacking the trailing `moved && ValidateParent()` that PublishFirstNoReplace:530 and MoveNoReplace:692 perform. NARROWED: a redirected exchange cannot land silently, because the very next step re-inspects through the retained parent handle and requires `FileHandleIdentity.IdentitiesMatch(created.Metadata.Identity, landed.Canonical.Metadata.Identity)` at FileStore.cs:665-690, so the outcome is RecoveryRequired/Unavailable rather than a publication into an attacker's tree; the DACL transplant is likewise repaired by ApplyOwnerOnlyAndVerify at FileStore.cs:701. What survives is the broken anchoring invariant itself, plus the non-adversarial MAX_PATH band — the parent path must still be short enough for OpenParentNoFollow's CreateFileW at :1122, so only parent+leaf over MAX_PATH breaks, and only when long-path support is off.

summary: OpenAtUnix is declared as a fixed-arity P/Invoke to the variadic libc `openat`, so on Apple ARM64 — where the platform ABI requires variadic arguments to be passed on the stack rather than in registers — the 0600 creation mode passed at line 1215 may not reach the callee's va_arg, and the exclusively created working file exists with an unintended (umask-masked) mode until Fchmod repairs it at line 451.
failure_scenario: openat is `int openat(int, const char *, int, ...)`; the mode is a variadic argument. Apple's arm64 ABI deviates from AAPCS64 and passes variadic arguments on the stack, while this declaration places the mode in x3. If the callee reads the stack, the created mode is whatever the stack held, masked by the process umask — typically yielding 0755/0644 rather than 0600. Between CreateWorkingExclusive's openat at :1211 and the Fchmod at :451 (and the write of the journal bytes at Store:530), another local user can open the file read-only and hold the descriptor across the chmod, then read the published envelope. Every subsequent check passes because they inspect the post-fchmod mode, so no test can observe this. Note the same declaration shape exists at src/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Infrastructure/Security/FileHandleIdentity.cs:1636, so if real this is repo-wide rather than local to this file. Linux is unaffected.
verifier_reason: Settled empirically rather than left speculative. Disassembling this machine's own /usr/lib/system/libsystem_kernel.dylib (arm64) shows `_openat` reading the mode from the CALLER'S STACK: `tbnz w2, #0x9` (test O_CREAT=0x200 in flags) -> `ldr w23, [x29, #0x10]` -> `and w3, w23, #0xffff` -> `bl ___openat`; x3 as supplied by the caller is overwritten and never read. The macOS create path does set that bit — Primitives.cs:1181-1187 `flags |= 0x00000200 | 0x00000800` — so the fixed-arity `OpenAtUnix(int, string, int, int)` at :1863-1864 delivers unspecified stack contents as the creation mode at :1211-1215, and Fchmod at :451 is the only thing that ever establishes 0600. NARROWED on both of the finder's supporting claims: the repo does NOT rely on this shape elsewhere — FileHandleIdentity.cs:1639's twin always passes `mode: 0` with flag sets that never include O_CREAT (:635-639, :837-841, :939-943, constants :1479-1493), so that site is unaffected; and the cross-user read is blocked, because every operation first runs ValidateParent() (:1035-1042) -> HasStrictOwnerOnlyParentHandlePosture (:1078-1105) requiring the parent directory to be exactly 0700 and owned by the euid, so no other unprivileged user can traverse in during the window. Confirmed separately: no test observes the pre-fchmod mode — File.GetUnixFileMode appears nowhere under tests/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Tests/GrimoireTransitions/.
verifier_worse: The finder hedged with 'may not reach the callee's va_arg' and predicted a umask-masked 0755/0644; in fact the mode never reaches the kernel at all and the value used is an arbitrary 32-bit word masked only by umask and ALLPERMS — which on BSD can include S_ISUID/S_ISGID, bits umask does not strip. The finder's 'repo-wide' note is the one part that is wrong: FileHandleIdentity.cs is unaffected.

summary: CompareUnlink requires the retained handle to report HardLinkCount == 0 after the delete, but on Windows the delete is a FILE_DISPOSITION_POSIX_SEMANTICS disposition set on a still-open handle, and if NTFS keeps reporting nNumberOfLinks == 1 until the last handle closes then every retirement and every delete returns Data.RecoveryRequired on Windows.
failure_scenario: Store:1383 (CompleteRetirementAsync) and Store:1808 (RetireAsync, reached from both ReplaceDurablyAsync:757 and DeleteDurably:894) both fail closed on CompareUnlink. The post-condition at :889-898 re-reads metadata through GetFileInformationByHandle (Security/FileHandleIdentity.cs:1199-1210) on `expected.Handle` — the same handle that is keeping the deleted file object alive. If that reports 1 rather than 0, the whole retirement/delete family is permanently broken on Windows while every Unix run is green; nothing in the suite would catch it, since no test in this file executes on Windows semantics (see D3-5). The Unix branch is unaffected: unlinkat drops the link immediately and fstat reports 0.
verifier_reason: The code is exactly as cited: Primitives.cs:855-861 sets `FileDispositionDelete | FileDispositionPosixSemantics` through SetFileInformationByHandle on `expected.Handle`, and :889-898 re-reads that same still-open handle and fails closed on `|| after.HardLinkCount != 0`, with FileStore.cs:1383 and :1808 both mapping the failure to Data.RecoveryRequired. Saying it plainly: this cannot be settled read-only from macOS. Documented semantics argue against the hypothesis rather than for it — FILE_DISPOSITION_FLAG_POSIX_SEMANTICS is specified as removing the name from the directory namespace immediately (only the data survives until the last handle closes), and NTFS maintains a genuine hard-link count, so nNumberOfLinks reaching 0 is the expected reading; Microsoft does not, however, document nNumberOfLinks in the delete-pending state. The repository offers no cross-check: this is the only `HardLinkCount != 0` requirement in src/ (every other check requires ==1), and no test in tests/ reaches it. summary: A missing anti-rollback anchor is treated as "never provisioned" even when the profile's journal key already exists, so the monotonic slot epoch silently resets to zero instead of failing closed.
failure_scenario: Profile has run operations through slot epoch 5 (Closed anchor + retained stable key, per design §3 'retains the stable key and a terminal anchor tombstone'). The anchor credential is then lost or removed on its own — keychain item purge, Windows Credential Manager cleanup, credential-store migration, or a deleter who cannot read/forge entries. Next BeginAsync reads no anchor (`existing is null`), calls `_keys.CreateOrOpen` which happily returns the pre-existing key without signalling that it pre-existed, writes a fresh `SlotEpoch: 0` closed genesis (AnchorStore.cs:137) and opens epoch 1 again. Slot epochs 1..5 are now reusable under the same AES-256-GCM key, so the (key, slotEpoch, operationId, kind, revision, previousDigest) AAD tuples of the earlier era can recur exactly; with the design's stable, database-derived operation id an old sealed envelope becomes cryptographically admissible again. RecoverAsync:825 has the mirror hole: anchor absent + files absent returns NoActiveJournal (readiness proceeds) rather than refusing. The sibling implementation of this exact pattern does refuse: InstallationResetActiveStore.cs:924 treats file-absent-but-key-present as `EvidenceFailure()`.
verifier_reason: Re-derived every step: GrimoireOfflineTransitionJournalStore.cs:282 `if (existing is null)` requires only `AllAbsent(evidence)` (:285), then :292 `_keys.CreateOrOpen` returns a pre-existing key silently (KeyProvider.cs:69-74 `if (existing.Value is { } stored) return ...Mint(stored);`), :313 writes a `SlotEpoch: 0` Closed genesis (AnchorStore.cs:137) and :402 `nextEpoch = checked(existing.SlotEpoch + 1)` reopens epoch 1. RecoverAsync:825-833 is the mirror: `return AllAbsent(evidence) ? ...NoActiveJournal : RecoveryRequired`, and spec:259-262 says NoActiveJournal permits readiness. The spec does not sanction this: :105-107 removes key and anchor together only in full installation reset, and :131 says the first operation compares from 'the exact provisioned closed genesis anchor'. `GrimoireOfflineTransitionJournalKeyProvider.IsPresent` (KeyProvider.cs:139) exists for exactly this check and has zero callers anywhere in src/ or tests/, while the sibling refuses the same shape at InstallationResetActiveStore.cs:924.
verifier_worse: The finder asserted replay admissibility without naming the admitting site; it is constructible at AuthenticateOneAhead:1451-1477, which accepts a file at `decoded.Value.Revision != anchor.Revision + 1` with `PreviousEnvelopeDigest != previous` where `previous = ZeroDigest` when `anchor.Revision == 0`, matching only (profile, installation, SlotEpoch, OperationId, Kind, PayloadVersion, location) — every one of which recurs exactly after the epoch reset when the same database-derived operation is retried. A retained pre-deletion epoch-1/revision-1 envelope therefore authenticates under the same key in the reopened rev-0 one-ahead window and AuthenticateEvidence advances the anchor onto it. Note the narrower converse: once the new era publishes a revision, the anchor's fresh EnvelopeDigest does reject the old file, so the exposure is the crash/opening window, not steady state.

summary: Nonces are 96 random bits under a key that is never rotated, while the code's own caps admit up to 10^12 seals per key — eight orders of magnitude past the NIST SP 800-38D limit for random GCM IVs.
failure_scenario: MaxSlotEpoch (1e6, line 42) x MaxRevision (1e6, line 40) = 10^12 permitted Seal calls, and the key is explicitly stable across every slot epoch (design §3: 'retains the stable key'; the provider has no rotate path). SP 800-38D caps random-IV GCM at 2^32 invocations per key; at 2^40 messages the birthday probability of a repeated 96-bit nonce is roughly 2^-17, and a single nonce+key repeat leaks the XOR of two journal plaintexts and, worse, the GHASH authentication subkey, permitting forged envelopes. There is no persisted counter, which is the right call for crash safety (a crash cannot reuse a nonce because nothing is derived from durable state) — the gap is purely the missing per-epoch key derivation or seal budget. This compounds D4-1: an epoch reset makes the whole AAD tuple, not just the nonce, repeat.
verifier_reason: Authenticator.cs:159 `byte[] nonce = RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(NonceBytes);` with `NonceBytes = 12` (:28) under a key with no rotate path (KeyProvider.cs exposes only CreateOrOpen/OpenExisting/IsPresent) and spec:106 'retains the stable key'. The declared caps are real: `MaxRevision = 1_000_000` (:40) enforced at :629, `MaxSlotEpoch = 1_000_000` (:42) enforced at store:412, so the *permitted* seal count per key is 10^12 ≈ 2^40, past the SP 800-38D 2^32 random-IV limit. NARROWED: this is a bound-hygiene defect, not a reachable risk — every Seal is an fsync'd file publication under an exclusive maintenance lock, so any realistic workload stays at or below MaxRevision within one epoch (collision probability ≈ 2^-57). What survives is that the code's own asserted limits do not imply the cryptographic bound they need.

suggested_fix: Derive a per-slot-epoch subkey (HKDF over the stable key with the slot epoch as info) so no key ever sees more than MaxRevision seals, or lower MaxSlotEpoch x MaxRevision below 2^32 and assert the product.
test_to_write: An arithmetic guard test asserting `MaxSlotEpoch * MaxRevision <= 2^32` for a stable key, or that Seal at epoch E and epoch E+1 use different key material.

summary: The AES-256 journal key transits immutable managed strings on both write and read, defeating the file's own careful `CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory` discipline on every byte array.

summary: The web factory replaces the host's pooled, singleton-options composition with the CLI-shaped `AddDbContext`, so every web-factory test runs a per-scope `CovenantConnectionEnrolmentInterceptor` and a fresh connection per request, and the two composition tests added to guard this cannot detect the difference.

The fixture registers `services.AddDbContext<ArcanumDbContext>((sp, options) => ...)` at ArcanumWebApplicationFactory.cs:179 (options lifetime Scoped, so the `(sp, options)` lambda mints a fresh `new CovenantConnectionEnrolmentInterceptor(...)` at :184 per scope), while the host uses `services.AddDbContextPool<ArcanumDbContext>(...poolSize: 32)` at ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:1121, which forces singleton options and therefore exactly one interceptor. summary: On a client disconnect the streaming tool loop abandons its iterator at a `yield return` inside the ward pump and never awaits `processTask`, so a running MCP tool call outlives the guarantee that the turn producer has finished.
failure_scenario: Streaming turn, model calls a slow tool (execute_command / ask_human / apply_patch). While `PumpWardAndHumanEventsAsync` is yielding ward/HITL frames (3567), the client socket dies. InferenceExecuteWriter cancels `streamCts`, TurnExecutionCoordinator.JoinProducerAsync cancels and awaits the producer, TurnEngine.RunTurnCoreAsync awaits the pipeline runner — all of which unwind through this iterator's `finally` blocks. The `finally` at 3651 disposes only `askHumanReservation`; `processTask` (created 3552, awaited only at 3571 on the happy path) is left running. TurnEngine therefore reports 'producer observed' while an MCP tool call is still executing, and the tool's own Grimoire writes (GrimoirePendingReceiptSink → grimoireTurnWriter, PersistedToolInvocationAmbient scope) race the outer `finally`'s `TryResolveInterruptedOnStreamExitAsync` (4204) and the request-scoped DbContext that ASP.NET disposes and re-leases the moment the endpoint returns — the exact hazard TurnExecutionCoordinator.cs:218-226 documents as the reason it waits for the producer.
verifier_reason: Re-derived every `finally` inside RunInferenceAttemptAsync (1546-4216): only 3252, 3546, 3651, 3667, 4160 exist, and none observes `processTask` (declared 3552, awaited only at 3571). The orphan window is open because `TurnEventEmitter.EmitAsync` catches only ChannelClosedException (:76) and ObjectDisposedException (:80) — not OperationCanceledException — so `await _channel.Writer.WriteAsync(evt, cancellationToken)` (:67) throws OCE the instant TurnExecutionCoordinator.JoinProducerAsync cancels (:243), unwinding RunStreamingIntoEmitterAsync's `await foreach`, which disposes StreamPromptCoreAsync's enumerator, whose `finally { await enumerator.DisposeAsync(); }` (:1440-1442, and :1094-1096 on the single-lease path) disposes RunInferenceAttemptAsync at `yield return liveEvent` (:3567) and runs 3651/3667/4160 with the tool task still running. Narrowed to the state where a ward/HITL frame is in flight: with no frame pending the pump instead spins (see worse_than_reported) and does join the task.
verifier_worse: Two things. summary: The macOS dynamic-dependency check prints `ok: links only its declared dynamic dependencies` on empty input — `|| true` swallows a missing `otool`, and every `@rpath/` dependency is filtered out before comparison, so a dynamically linked libcrypto is exactly the shape the check cannot see.

If `otool` is absent (it is not in the script's `require_cmd jq awk` list at :740), or if `grep -v` filters everything, `actual` is empty; the `while` loop's `[ -z "${dependency}" ] && continue` skips the only iteration, `unexpected` stays 0, and line 637 prints `ok`. The manifest's whole claim for osx-arm64 is `dynamicDependencies: ["/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib"]` with `openssl.linkage: "static"`; a build that accidentally linked OpenSSL dynamically with `-rpath` emits `@rpath/libcrypto.3.dylib`, which this filter removes, and the script then reports all checks passed. Separately, the win-* branch (:643-647) performs no dependency comparison at all, so the manifest's `dynamicDependencies` for win-x64/win-arm64 (ADVAPI32.dll, KERNEL32.dll, bcrypt.dll) is asserted by nothing on any platform.

summary: The AOT IL gate fails closed on a second consecutive run against a warm tree: MSBuild skips `IlcCompile` when the publish is up to date, so the log contains no ILC marker and `assert_log_has_ilc_output` refuses to report a pass.
failure_scenario: A developer follows AGENTS.md:32 and runs `./scripts/verify-aot-il-warnings.sh`. The first run publishes and passes. Nothing is edited; the second run's `dotnet publish` is incremental — `IlcCompile` and the ILC link are skipped, so neither 'Generating native code' nor 'ILC :' nor 'ilc.rsp' appears in `$cli_log` (or in the regex smoke's `$smoke_log`, whose `-o` is a fresh mktemp -d but whose `obj/` is not). `assert_log_has_ilc_output` (:332, called at :481 and :493) returns 1, `run_single_rid` returns 1, and the script exits 1 with 'AOT IL gate failed: cannot verify the CLI closure on RID …' — a message that reads as an AOT defect when the tree is clean. The workaround (`dotnet clean` or deleting obj/bin) is not documented anywhere.
verifier_reason: The mechanism is real and the citations are exact: publish_cli_rid builds `publish_args=(publish "$PROJECT" -c Release -r "$rid")` with no `-o` and no `--no-incremental`, publish_regex_smoke_rid uses a fresh `mktemp -d` for `-o` but shares the project's obj/, and assert_log_has_ilc_output:332 `if ! markers="$(rg_capture "Generating native code|ILC :|ilc\.rsp" "$log")"` returns 1 with 'refusing to report a pass' when the markers are absent. The repository names the same hazard itself at ci.yml:210 — 'an incremental build hides the analyzer diagnostics a clean one raises' — and fixes it there with `--no-incremental` (ci.yml:217), which is exactly the guard the AOT gate lacks. I marked this PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED because the brief forbids running dotnet, so I could not observe MSBuild actually skipping IlcCompile on a warm tree. The gate fails closed, so there is no false pass; the cost is a confusing 'AOT IL gate failed: cannot verify the CLI closure' on a clean tree with an undocumented workaround.
verifier_worse: The same incrementality would also suppress the Roslyn IL analyzer diagnostics that count_il_violations (:402) scans for, so if the ILC markers ever did survive a warm run, the gate would report 0 violations against a log in which no analyzer ran. The fail-closed assert at :332 is the only thing standing between this and a false PASS.
production_path: AGENTS.md:32 -> scripts/verify-aot-il-warnings.sh main -> run_single_rid -> publish_rid -> publish_cli_rid (incremental) -> :481/:493 assert_log_has_ilc_output -> :332. Verified as written; the incremental-skip step is inferred, not observed.
suggested_fix: Publish into a per-run `mktemp -d` output *and* pass `-p:IntermediateOutputPath` / `--no-incremental` (or delete `obj/Release/$rid` for the two projects) so ILC always runs; alternatively accept 'Skipping target "IlcCompile"' as positive evidence that an ILC-capable publish was configured.
test_to_write: A shell test that drives the gate twice against the same stub log directory and asserts the second run's exit status equals the first — RED today.

summary: `count_il_violations` tests the third-party allow-list before it tests first-party ownership, and the allow-list matches the warning *message*, so a genuine first-party IL warning whose message names an EF Core or Serilog member is silently dropped.
failure_scenario: First-party code calls an EF Core API annotated `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]`, e.g. `src/.../Grimoire/X.cs(10,5): warning IL2026: Using member 'Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Query.QueryCompiler.Execute<TResult>(Expression)' which has 'RequiresUnreferencedCodeAttribute' [.../RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Infrastructure.csproj]`. The origin is a first-party `.cs(` path, so `il_warning_is_first_party` would return true — but line 414 short-circuits first: `il_warning_is_allowed` matches 'Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore' in the message and `continue`s, so the violation is never counted and the gate prints PASS. The gate's own comment at :367-370 justifies message-matching as fixing the inverse bug (allow tokens hitting first-party file *paths*), and the self-test verify_aot_il_warnings_test.sh:74-79 pins only that path case; the message case has no test at all.
verifier_reason: The ordering is exactly as cited — :414 `if il_warning_is_allowed "$line"; then` / :415 `continue` precedes :418 `if il_warning_is_first_party "$line"; then`. But the finder's own example is arguably the intended behaviour: the comment at :367-369 says 'The ALLOWED tokens name third-party components that own a warning, so they may only be matched against the message', and their suggested fix (classify ownership first) would break that intent and red every EF-Core-owned warning. What survives is a different, constructible false negative: il_warning_message (:356-364) returns everything after `warning ILNNNN:`, which for IL2026 is the *offending member name*, so a genuinely first-party warning naming a first-party type whose name contains an allow token is dropped. Those types exist — src/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Infrastructure/Logging/ contains SerilogLogRingBufferSink.cs, HostLockSerilogFileSink.cs and SecureSerilogFileHooks.cs. That is the same bug class the comment claims to have fixed, moved from the file path to the member name, and verify_aot_il_warnings_test.sh:74 pins only the path case (its message names `System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize`, which contains no token).
production_path: .github/workflows/ci.yml:206 (macos-workspace-check) and :489 (aot-il) -> scripts/verify-aot-il-warnings.sh:502 (count_il_violations) -> :414 (il_warning_is_allowed, message-substring) -> :415 continue. Verified.
suggested_fix: Swap the order: classify ownership by origin first, and only consult the ALLOWED message tokens for warnings whose origin is `ILC :` or a project file (i.e. warnings with no first-party source location).
test_to_write: Add to verify_aot_il_warnings_test.sh a case whose origin is `/repo/src/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Infrastructure/Grimoire/X.cs(10,5)` and whose IL2026 message names `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore`, asserting count == 1 — it returns 0 today.

summary: The script's own documented no-argument invocation aborts on macOS: `"${host_args[@]}"` expands an empty array under `set -u`, which bash 3.2 (the stock macOS and GitHub macOS-runner shell) rejects as an unbound variable.
failure_scenario: A developer runs the documented `./scripts/benchmark-covenant.sh` (usage line 5, 'measure and report'). `host_args=()` at :100 stays empty because no flag was passed; `set -euo pipefail` is in force from :84; bash 3.2 evaluates `"${host_args[@]}"` at :177 as `host_args[@]: unbound variable` and the script exits 1 *after* a full Native AOT publish of the benchmark host, reporting nothing and printing no benchmark. CI never sees this because ci.yml:225 always passes `--gate --record`. This repository already documents this exact bash-3.2 hazard and uses the guard form elsewhere — common.sh:274 `"${MACHO_PATHS_ORDERED[@]+\"${MACHO_PATHS_ORDERED[@]}\"}"` and release-macos-arm64.yml:333-338 — so the fix pattern is already house style.
verifier_reason: Reproduced on this machine: `command -v bash` resolves to /bin/bash, `/bin/bash --version` reports 3.2.57(1)-release, and `/bin/bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; a=(); printf "%s\n" "${a[@]}"'` exits 1 with `a[@]: unbound variable`, while the guarded form `${a[@]+"${a[@]}"}` exits 0. scripts/benchmark-covenant.sh:177 is `"$EXECUTABLE" "${host_args[@]}"`, host_args is initialised empty at :100 and appended to only under --gate (:108), --record (:117) and --compare (:126), and `set -euo pipefail` at :84 is never relaxed before :177. The narrowing is the shebang: it is `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, not `#!/bin/bash`, so a developer with Homebrew bash 5 ahead of /bin on PATH is unaffected — but on a stock Mac, and on this repo's own machine, it aborts after the full Native AOT publish of the benchmark host. CI never sees it (ci.yml:225 always passes `--gate --record`). The guard form is already house style at scripts/packaging/macos/common.sh:274 and :319 and .github/workflows/release-macos-arm64.yml:199,338.
production_path: scripts/benchmark-covenant.sh:5 (documented `./scripts/benchmark-covenant.sh` — 'measure and report') -> :84 (set -euo pipefail) -> :100 (host_args=()) -> :177. Verified by executing the equivalent expansion under /bin/bash 3.2.57.
suggested_fix: Change line 177 to `"$EXECUTABLE" ${host_args[@]+"${host_args[@]}"}`, matching the guard already used at scripts/packaging/macos/common.sh:274 and .github/workflows/release-macos-arm64.yml:338.

failure_scenario: build-arcanum.sh:131-147 counts managed assemblies and, under ARCANUM_REQUIRE_MACOS_AOT (set at release-macos-arm64.yml:250), fails the release when the publish is the CoreCLR fallback, with the comment 'every check below passes on the fallback'. package-windows.ps1 has no equivalent: `Publish-Cli` publishes at :185, `Assert-StagedNatives` at :208 checks only that e_sqlcipher.dll and libonigwrap.dll are present (both are present in the fallback too), and the zip ships. build-windows.yml:78-82 states the risk explicitly ('a publish that cannot find those tools does not fail — it falls back to a self-contained CoreCLR folder that packages, ships, and is quietly no longer Native AOT') and mitigates it only by choosing a native runner, without asserting the result. A future `-p:PublishAot=false`, a condition change in Cli.csproj:36-38, or a missing ILCompiler package for win-arm64 would ship a non-AOT `arcanum.exe` labelled Native AOT in the release notes (release.yml:325).

Narrowed because the fallback it would catch is asserted only by the repo's own prose (build-windows.yml:77-82, docs/Arcanum.DESIGN.md:4131) and I could not demonstrate it occurs — Cli.csproj:36 sets PublishAot unconditionally for any non-Apple RID with a RuntimeIdentifier, and a Windows AOT publish without the MSVC linker normally errors rather than degrading. Latent defence-in-depth gap, not a defect present today.

summary: TryGetSttySize drains both child pipes with blocking ReadToEnd() before it ever reaches WaitForExit(1000), so the 1-second timeout and the Kill fallback are unreachable dead code and a wedged `stty` hangs Command Center startup forever.
failure_scenario: `stty size` is started with stdin inherited from the terminal. If the controlling tty is in a state where stty blocks (a stopped/orphaned pty, a hung terminal emulator), `process.StandardOutput.ReadToEnd()` on line 269 blocks the calling thread indefinitely. Control never reaches `process.WaitForExit(1000)` on line 271, so the timeout and the `process.Kill(entireProcessTree: true)` recovery below it can never fire. `arcanum` Command Center hangs at viewport detection with no output. Secondarily, reading stdout to EOF before touching stderr is the classic pipe-buffer deadlock shape; it is benign only because `stty size` writes a few bytes.

The ProcessStartInfo at :253-260 sets RedirectStandardOutput/RedirectStandardError/UseShellExecute/CreateNoWindow but NOT RedirectStandardInput, so the child inherits the controlling tty. A `stty` that stops (SIGTTIN in a background process group, an orphaned or wedged pty) never exits and never closes its stdout write end, so ReadToEnd() blocks the calling thread forever and control never reaches the 1-second deadline or `process.Kill(entireProcessTree: true)` at :277 — both are unreachable on that path.
verifier_worse: Yes. The exposure is per-iteration and recurs after startup, not once.

With a proxy in front, Connection.RemoteIpAddress is the proxy's address for every request, so ResolveRateLimitPartitionKey yields one key `ip:<proxy>` and the fixed-window PermitLimit is shared by all callers: one noisy client 429s everyone else, and per-caller limiting — the stated purpose — never happens. `grep -rn UseForwardedHeaders src/` matches only compiled dSYM symbol tables, never a source registration.

summary: Every identity predicate in both retention partials wraps the column in `lower(replace(col,'-',''))`, and no expression index matching that shape exists anywhere under Schema/**, so each such predicate is a full table scan.

summary: TryQuarantineOwnedFile validates only file identity and hard-link count against its journal, never mtime or length, and unlike the log path performs no post-quarantine freshness re-check, so a file rewritten in place after its snapshot is quarantined and deleted as if unchanged.

An in-place rewrite of an attachment or uploaded file between PrepareMutationJournalAsync (DataRetentionService.cs:6084) and TryQuarantineOwnedFile keeps the same volume serial + file index, so `expected.Metadata != artifact.Metadata` is false and the new bytes are deleted. DeleteLogCandidate (Pruning.cs:6696) closes the same window by re-reading `quarantined.LastWriteTimeUtc` after the rename and restoring the file when it is fresher than the cutoff; the attachment/uploaded-file path has no equivalent. In this slice the governing DB row is deleted in the same transaction, which bounds the damage — the unbounded form is the disk-vs-DB attachment orphan sweep outside this slice.

PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED because the in-place-rewrite timing between PrepareMutationJournalAsync (:6084, called at :914) and the quarantine is a race I cannot construct from the code. DOWNGRADED to minor on the finder's own bound: all three in-slice callers (:2629, :2941, Pruning.cs:5619) delete the governing DB row in the same transaction, so the artifact was going regardless. This is known-issue-233 territory as tagged.
production_path: DataRetentionEndpoints.cs:216 (DELETE /data/attachments/{id}) -> DataRetentionService.cs:694 -> :723 -> :2941 TryQuarantineOwnedFile -> :6460 -> :6530. The unbounded orphan-sweep form the finder points at lives in the attachment store, outside this slice, and I did not verify it.
suggested_fix: Carry LastWriteTimeUtc and Length in the journal entry and re-verify them after the quarantine rename in TryQuarantineOwnedFile, restoring the file when they no longer match — the same shape DeleteLogCandidate already uses.

summary: The published source-definition fingerprint is SHA-256 over the raw `.sql` text including comments and indentation, so a comment-only edit to any core schema file changes CoreSchemaFingerprint and makes every already-installed Grimoire refuse to open.

On the next start, GrimoireSchemaEvolutionPlanner.Decide (GrimoireSchemaEvolutionPlanner.cs:114-121) compares the recorded fingerprint to the new one, they differ, and it returns Refused(SourceDefinitionMismatch). Core is the tier whose refusal aborts startup (GrimoireSchemaInstaller.cs:331-336 throws GrimoireSchemaRefusedException for the Core tier), so the host and every CLI verb that opens the Grimoire go down for a change that altered no SQL. GrimoireSqlNormalizer already strips comments, but it is used only for the per-object manifest, never for the fingerprint.
verifier_reason: GrimoireSchemaCatalog.cs:680 is `.Append(definition.Sql)` — the raw unresolved text — inside ComputeSourceFingerprint (:661), whose own doc says 'before its exact unresolved SQL' (:658-660). GrimoireSqlNormalizer is called only from GrimoireSchemaManifestInspector.cs:401, CovenantAcceleratorSyntheticManifest.cs:63 and GrimoireSchemaManifestBuilder.cs:93/:295 — never from the fingerprint. GrimoireSchemaVersionChain.cs:194-195 returns the *computed* HeadManifest fingerprint for the head version, and the head Core version is 5 (GrimoireSchemaVersionChains.cs:45) whose fingerprint is not pinned to any literal — `SourcePins` (:63-113) carries literals only for versions 2/3/4, and the two tests touching CoreSchemaFingerprint (GrimoireSchemaEvolutionFixture.cs:152, GrimoireSchemaTransitionResourceTests.cs:293) compare it to the same computed value. So a comment-only edit ships: Planner.cs:114-121 refuses SourceDefinitionMismatch and GrimoireSchemaInstaller.cs:336 throws GrimoireSchemaRefusedException for the Core tier. Known-issue-224 verbatim; it fails closed, so no data loss.

suggested_fix: Feed each statement through GrimoireSqlNormalizer.Normalize before appending to the fingerprint frame, keeping the family/tier/path/name prefix as-is.

summary: SqliteBusyRetry has no attempt cap and no deadline — it retries SQLITE_BUSY/LOCKED forever at a 2 s ceiling, bounded only by the caller's cancellation token, so a connection holding `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE` hangs every Grimoire call in the process instead of failing them.
failure_scenario: CovenantSqliteConnectionInitializer.cs:253-258 sets `PRAGMA locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE` for ExclusiveMaintenance mode. While that handle is held, every other connection gets SQLITE_BUSY after its 30 s-class busy_timeout. All 155 production call sites of SqliteBusyRetry (verified: every one passes a real token, none passes CancellationToken.None) then loop indefinitely. An HTTP request with no server-side timeout, or a hosted worker with a lifetime token, never returns and never surfaces a maintenance-unavailable error — it just stops responding. The type's own doc comment discusses metrics but never a bound.
verifier_reason: SqliteBusyRetry.cs:45 is `while (true)` with no attempt cap and no deadline; the `if (attempt < int.MaxValue)` at :74 is overflow protection, not a bound, and the only exit is `Task.Delay(delay, cancellationToken)` at :64 throwing. `PRAGMA locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE` at CovenantSqliteConnectionInitializer.cs:253-258 is reached from CovenantCanonicalErasureTransaction.cs:191 and CovenantLocalErasureStorageHealth.cs:1709, both registered as singletons in the serving container (ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:1765-1782) and consumed by CovenantErasureTransition.cs:31 — so this is not offline-only. No ASP.NET request timeout is configured (`grep -rn 'AddRequestTimeouts|UseRequestTimeouts|RequestTimeout' src/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Api` returns only two 408 status-code mappings), so an in-flight request's token cancels only on client disconnect. This is tracker 251's territory (maintenance-unavailable HTTP responses).
production_path: src/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Infrastructure/Data/SqliteBusyRetry.cs:37-82, entered from e.g. SessionEntryPersistence.cs:483 and LongRunningOperationStore.cs:91; exclusive holder reachable via ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:1775 -> CovenantLocalErasureStorageHealth.cs:1709 -> CovenantSqliteConnectionInitializer.cs:253-258
suggested_fix: Add a total-deadline parameter (defaulting to a few multiples of BusyTimeoutMs) and throw a typed 'Grimoire temporarily unavailable' error when it elapses, so the endpoint layer can map it to a maintenance-unavailable response.
test_to_write: Call ExecuteAsync with an action that always throws SqliteException(5) and a token that is never cancelled, under a test deadline — the call should fail with a bounded-retry error rather than run until the test times out.

A `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM LongRunningOperations WHERE SessionId = Sessions.Id AND State IN (active))` written the obvious way is always true, and the retention sweep deletes sessions with a live operation attached.

summary: On the ReplacedButUnverified path AtomicFile deliberately leaves a `.arcanum-bak-<guid>` (or `.arcanum-quarantine-<guid>`) file behind 'for operator recovery', but AtomicReplaceStatus is a bare enum with no path, so no caller can tell the operator where the backup is and nothing ever sweeps them.

The caller — e.g. PhysicalFileSystemWriter.cs:483, writing into the user's own workspace — receives an enum value and reports a generic failure. A randomly named hidden file remains in the destination directory forever, and repeated failures accumulate them. PhysicalWorkspaceScanner will then also enumerate them as workspace content.

Two sub-claims are wrong, though. PhysicalFileSystemWriter.cs:510-512 does not report 'a generic failure' — it returns a distinct message, 'The file was replaced but post-move verification failed; the destination was left in an unverified state.' And PhysicalWorkspaceScanner will not enumerate the artifacts: PhysicalWorkspaceScanner.cs:131-134 skips every entry whose extension is not `.sln`. summary: The Covenant selective-import loop commits each Session under its own lease with no outer transaction, so a per-Session refusal after the first commit returns a zero-count `Failed` result that the restore reports as `Rejected` — the status that means nothing was changed.
failure_scenario: `arcanum backup restore x.arcabak --conflict-mode import-selected-sessions --session-id A --session-id B --session-id C` with Covenant enabled. Session C is source-tainted (or its `AcquireProtectedTransferAsync` lease is contended, or `CompleteAsync` fails), so `ImportOneProtectedAsync` returns a failure. `ImportProtectedAsync` discards the running counts and returns `BackupSessionImportResult.Failed(...)` (Sessions=0), `ImportSelectedSessionsAsync` turns that into `Rejected`, and the CLI prints `Restore: REJECTED` with exit 1. The live Grimoire now permanently holds A and B — under fresh identities — and the operator's documented remedy (re-run the import) imports them a second time. The coverage preflight added at lines 84-105 fixes only the unmapped-Campaign case; every other per-Session refusal still lands here.

summary: Extraction tracks observed entries with `StringComparer.Ordinal` and writes each one with `FileMode.Create`, so two archive entries whose paths differ only in case silently collapse into one file on a case-insensitive destination while the manifest comparison still passes.
failure_scenario: An archive is created on Linux from an installation holding two attachments recorded as `attachments/2026/Report.pdf` and `attachments/2026/report.pdf` (attachment relative paths come from the database and are user-derived — BackupInventoryPlanner.cs:556/583). Both survive `ValidateManifest`'s strict-ordinal ordering. Restoring on macOS/APFS or Windows: the second `CreateOwnerOnlyTempFile(destination)` truncates and overwrites the first, but `entries` still records both with the hashes computed from the *stream*, so `CompareManifest` sees two intact entries and reports zero issues. `ComposeStagedTree` (BackupRestoreService.cs:1828) then copies the same on-disk bytes into two colliding staged destinations, and `ValidateStagedGenerationAsync` finds both `File.Exists`. The restore reports Completed while one attachment now silently carries the other's bytes.
verifier_reason: Every link re-derived. Extraction tracks observed entries in `Dictionary<string, ObservedEntry> entries = new(StringComparer.Ordinal);` (BackupArchiveCodec.cs:1994) and the per-entry duplicate guard is `entries.ContainsKey(record.Path)` (:2009) — exact-match only — then writes through `SecureFilePermissions.CreateOwnerOnlyTempFile(destination)` at :2067, which is `FileMode.Create` (SecureFilePermissions.cs:465-471), i.e. silent truncate-and-overwrite on a case-insensitive volume. `CompareManifest` (:2176-2216) compares the manifest against the in-memory `observed` hashes computed from the decrypted stream and never re-reads the destination, so both entries verify over one file; `ValidateStagedGenerationAsync` (BackupRestoreService.cs:1715-1740) only tests presence of each referenced path, no hash. The premise that case-only-differing archive paths are constructible is verified in the writer: attachment archive paths are `"attachments/" + relative` straight from the database (BackupInventoryPlanner.cs:583), and the stored relative path is `ownerSegment/logicalKey/v{n}/originalFileName` (SessionAttachmentStore.cs:2616-2630) where both the logical key and the file name are user-supplied and `SessionAttachmentPathSanitizer.TrySanitize` (Core/Storage/SessionAttachmentPathSanitizer.cs:44-90) strips characters but never changes case.
verifier_worse: The collision is not confined to attachments: ComposeStagedTree at BackupRestoreService.cs:1828 uses `File.Copy(source, destination, overwrite: true)`, so a case collision that survives extraction is overwritten a second time in staging without a diagnostic, and BackupRestoreLayout rewriting can map two distinct archive paths onto one staged destination independently of the extraction-root collision.
production_path: src/RetroDownfall.Arcanum.Infrastructure/Backup/BackupRestoreService.cs:741 ExecuteAsync → :903 `_codec.ExtractAsync(plan.ArchivePath, recoveryPassphrase, extractRoot, workRoot, ...)` → BackupArchiveCodec.cs:620 ExtractAsync → :665 ExtractPayloadAsync (declared :1979) → :2054 ResolveExtractionPath → :2067; then BackupRestoreService.cs:934 ComposeStagedTree (declared :1774) copies both manifest entries onto colliding staged destinations at :1828, and the restore reports Completed.
suggested_fix: Keep the ordinal dictionary for protocol correctness but add a second `OrdinalIgnoreCase` (plus NFC) set of resolved destination paths and refuse the archive as malformed on a collision; alternatively open the destination with `FileMode.CreateNew` so a collision surfaces as an IOException instead of a silent overwrite.

summary: `ComposeStagedTree` copies the entire restored generation with synchronous `File.Copy` and accepts no `CancellationToken`, so the second full-size copy of a multi-gigabyte Grimoire is uncancellable and blocks the async pipeline.
failure_scenario: A 30 GB restore. After `ExtractAsync` has already written 30 GB of plaintext into `work/extract`, `ComposeStagedTree` copies every manifest entry again into `staged/` using blocking `File.Copy` on the current thread, with no token threaded through the loop. Ctrl-C during that window is not observed until the whole tree has been copied — the operator sees a CLI that ignores cancellation for minutes and a second full-size write the extraction already paid for. `BackupRestoreCapacityPlanner` correctly reserves for both copies, so this is cost, not a capacity bug.

summary: The journal is written temp-then-rename with the file's own contents fsynced, but the containing directory is never fsynced, so a power loss immediately after a phase advance can lose the rename and leave the previous phase on disk.
failure_scenario: `journal = BackupRestoreJournal.Advance(staging.Path, journal, BackupRestorePhase.Commit)` (BackupRestoreService.cs:1073) returns, `Commit()` performs the first rename, and the machine loses power before the directory entry for the renamed journal reaches stable storage. summary: `list_directory`'s opaque continuation replays the entire recursive directory enumeration from the top of the tree on every page, making a full listing quadratic in the number of entries.
failure_scenario: Page size defaults to 500 (IntelligenceSettings.cs:21). That is ~10 million redundant directory-entry visits and ~200 full `OrderBy` sorts of every directory, plus a full `IsPathUnderWorkspaceWithSymlinkCheck` component walk per *directory* on every replay (the deferral at :764 only skips the walk for plain files). The code comment at :16-22 acknowledges the replay but the enumeration cost itself is not bounded.

The per-directory symlink component walk is re-paid too — :764 `if (isDirectory || continuationReached())` defers the walk only for plain files. Page size is a hard 500 (IntelligenceSettings.cs:21, sourced non-configurably at McpConnectionManager.Lifecycle.cs:541), so the paging is quadratic as claimed. NARROWED on severity, for three reasons a maintainer would raise: `IsListDirectorySkipFolder` (:800) prunes `node_modules`/`bin`/`obj`/`.git`, so realistic trees are far smaller than 100k; the deferral at :756-763 is an explicit, documented mitigation of exactly this replay; and the replay is load-bearing for the checkpoint contract the code enforces at :539-545 (a vanished checkpoint must be detectable and force a restart), so the finder's suggested seek-to-resume fix would have to preserve that property rather than simply replace the token.
verifier_worse: Marginally. The page break at :524-525 also fires on `materializedBytes + entryBytes > textBudget`, where textBudget is `min(toolOutputCap, maxJsonRpcLineBytes)/2` (:467-473). Deep trees with long paths therefore break pages well below 500 entries, producing more pages than the finder's 500-per-page arithmetic assumes and making the quadratic term correspondingly larger.

summary: A `notifications/cancelled` that arrives before its `tools/call` has registered its CancellationTokenSource is silently dropped, so the tool call runs to completion uncancelled.
failure_scenario: The read loop dispatches each inbound line on its own `Task.Run` (ArcanumInternalToolServer.cs:394) and tracks them in `_inFlightLineTasks`, so line ordering does not imply handler ordering. If the cancel notification's task reaches `HandleCancelledNotification` (:736) before the tools/call task reaches `_inFlightToolCalls.TryAdd` (:1114), `TryGetValue` misses and the notification returns with no record. The tools/call then registers and runs a long `execute_command` or `workspace_check` to completion with a token nobody will ever cancel — the caller sees the turn keep executing after it asked to stop.

There is no tombstone and no synchronization between the two. NARROWED twice. (a) The window is small: I grepped for awaits between `BuildToolsCallResponseAsync`'s entry (:1050) and :1114 and found none — the gating between them (:1084-1106) is all synchronous, so the race needs thread-pool scheduling to invert two tasks queued microseconds apart. (b) The consequence is smaller than stated: the finder says "the caller sees the turn keep executing after it asked to stop", but SdkMcpClientWrapper.cs:294-297 rethrows `OperationCanceledException` when `cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested`, so the caller *is* released. verifier_worse: The orphaned work compounds with W6-1. An `execute_command` whose cancellation is dropped has no wall-clock deadline of its own (Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan at ExecuteCommand.cs:177) and no CPU-time bound if it blocks rather than spins, so the orphaned child survives until connection disposal cancels `connectionToken` — not until some timer fires.
production_path: ArcanumInternalToolServer.cs:394 (Task.Run per inbound line) → :520-527 (notification branch) → :526 HandleCancelledNotification → :736 TryGetValue miss → :738 silent return; racing the sibling task's path :1050 → :1114 TryAdd.
suggested_fix: Record an early-cancel tombstone keyed by requestId (with the same TTL/sweep discipline as ExpiringRequestBindingStore) when the notification finds no in-flight entry, and have the tools/call path consult and consume it immediately after TryAdd.

summary: A regular, fully contained file with more than one hard link is rejected with the sandbox-escape message "That path would leave the workspace sandbox", which tells the model to change the path when no path can succeed.
failure_scenario: pnpm-managed `node_modules` (and any workspace using hard-linked build caches) stores package files as hard links, so `HardLinkCount > 1` is routine inside a real workspace. `read_file_chunk` on such a file fails `expectedMetadata.HardLinkCount != 1` and returns `PathEscapesSandboxMessage`: "That path would leave the workspace sandbox, so the operation was not performed. Please use a path relative to the workspace root." The path *is* relative and *is* inside the root, so the model's only available remediation — rewrite the path — cannot work, and it will loop or conclude the file does not exist. The same message is reused for four distinct causes (containment failure, non-regular file kind, hard-link aliasing, opened-handle identity mismatch).
verifier_reason: Re-derived: SandboxedFileIo.cs:54-63 rejects on a three-way disjunction — metadata lookup failure, `expectedMetadata.Kind != FileSystemObjectKind.RegularFile` (:57), and `|| expectedMetadata.HardLinkCount != 1` (:59) — and all three emit the same `ToolError(PathEscapesSandboxMessage)` at :62, whose text is "That path would leave the workspace sandbox, so the operation was not performed. Please use a path relative to the workspace root." (:458-459). The message is used at eleven sites in this file (:38,:47,:62,:117,:150,:229,:357,:374,:383,:395,:436), so the conflation is wider than the four causes the finder named. The remediation it prescribes is unreachable for a hard-linked, fully contained file: no relative path spelling of that inode has a link count of 1. NARROWED on how routine the trigger is. The finder's headline case is pnpm `node_modules`; I cannot verify pnpm's link behaviour from this repo, and on APFS its default import method prefers clonefile (which does not raise the link count), so "routine inside a real workspace" is a Linux/Windows claim rather than a macOS one. `list_directory` also prunes `node_modules` (FileTools.cs:800), so the model does not encounter such files by browsing — only by an explicit path. The check itself is deliberate and documented (docs/Arcanum.DESIGN.md:3024, "proves the target is a regular file with exactly one hard link **before** opening"), so the finding is correctly about the remediation text alone.
production_path: ArcanumInternalToolServer.FileTools.cs:88-98 (read_file_chunk) → SandboxedFileIo.cs:305 (TryOpenForRead) → :59 → :62; the same gate is on the replace_text_block read at FileTools.cs:250 and every write path in SandboxedFileIo.
suggested_fix: Split the message: keep PathEscapesSandboxMessage for containment failures and emit a distinct "this file has more than one hard link and cannot be read or written through the sandbox" text for the aliasing rejection, so the model stops retrying paths.
test_to_write: A test that creates a workspace file, adds a second hard link to it, calls read_file_chunk, and asserts the error text names hard links rather than a path escaping the sandbox.

On the next sweep `existing == lastWriteUtc` is true and the file is skipped, so semantic search keeps serving the pre-edit chunks indefinitely — until some later write moves the mtime.

Nothing else participates in the change key — the `FileHandleIdentity` captured at :1070 is passed to `IndexFileAsync` (:1097) for TOCTOU revalidation only, not compared here. What survives is the mtime-preserving case: `cp -p`, `rsync -a/-t`, `tar -x` or an archive restore that puts different content back at the previously-indexed mtime, and coarse-granularity mounts (HFS+/exFAT/SMB, 1-2 s). summary: ProbeReachable performs a synchronous, uncancellable, untimed secret_service_get_sync D-Bus round trip, and OsCredentialStore.IsAvailable re-invokes it after every Failed operation rather than once.
failure_scenario: Headless Linux with libsecret-1.so.0 present and no session bus. ProbeAvailable() succeeds (client-side allocation), so CreatePlatformStore selects PlatformOsCredentialStore whose IsAvailable is ProbeReachable. Every credential operation then returns Failed, which OsCredentialStore.Evidence maps to Unknown, so the very next IsAvailable question re-enters secret_service_get_sync with cancellable = nint.Zero — a call that may attempt a dbus autolaunch and has no bound. On the master-key bootstrap path this runs during `arcanum serve` startup with no timeout and no cancellation, and it repeats for the file-encryption key, the Campaign root-identity key, the marker store read, and every provider credential read. libsecret's service caching only helps once a service actually answers.

But the re-probe half is explicitly an accepted trade-off, not a defect: the class remarks at OsCredentialStore.cs:41-51 state "a failure clears the verdict rather than recording one, and the next question goes back to the backend's own reachability probe. Nothing is cached behind a timer, so there is no window in which a remembered answer contradicts the backend." That is the finder's suggested fix, refused by name. What survives is only that the probe is one more synchronous, uncancellable, untimed native call — and that is the shape of every operation in this store (`secret_password_lookup_sync` at LinuxOsCredentialStore.cs:124 is equally sync and equally untimed), so the probe is not a distinct defect class. Whether a missing session bus makes it hang depends on dbus autolaunch behaviour I cannot inspect from the tree.

summary: The Windows PEM rehydration path exports the TLS private key into a managed byte[] that is never zeroed, leaving the key in collectable managed memory for the life of the host.

summary: TryFindKey allocates and zeroes two byte arrays per candidate key on every encrypted-blob read, and the fixed-time comparison it pays for is defeated by the surrounding length check and early return.
failure_scenario: Every GetForReadAsync / PeekForReadAsync — one per attachment, upload, or batch-artifact read — walks the key ring encoding both the stored key id and the requested key id to fresh ASCII arrays, calls FixedTimeEquals, then zeroes both. On a rotated ring of N keys that is 2N allocations plus 2N zeroing passes per blob read, inside the gate, on a path that already leaves the gate before decrypting. The constant-time property is not obtained anyway: `expected.Length == actual.Length` short-circuits before FixedTimeEquals, and the loop returns on the first match, so both the length and the matching key's position are still timing-visible. summary: Dispose disposes every per-account SemaphoreSlim without waiting for or refusing in-flight operations, so a shutdown concurrent with a credential read or save turns into ObjectDisposedException or SemaphoreFullException from the finally block.

When the in-flight run finishes and advances the watermark, the queued duplicate re-enters, re-reads `GetUnsummarizedEntriesAsync`, and spends a full extraction prompt on whatever it finds — often the same page the first run had already partially covered. I could not isolate a divergent *output* (the paging query `LoadAfterWatermarkThroughTimestampGroup` handles the same-tick group correctly), so this is reported as cost, not corruption.

summary: The attachment path sanitizer trims leading dots but never trailing dots or trailing spaces, and its output is used verbatim as both a directory segment and the leaf filename, so two distinct logical keys collapse to one on-disk path on Windows.
failure_scenario: A caller attaches with logicalNameHint "notes." and later with "notes" in the same session. TrySanitize returns "notes." and "notes" (line 99 only TrimStart's, line 128 returns the candidate unchanged), so the Grimoire stores two distinct LogicalKey rows. BuildRelativePath makes `{sessionId:N}/notes./v1/{file}` and `{sessionId:N}/notes/v1/{file}`; Win32 strips the trailing dot at the filesystem layer, so both resolve to one directory and the second write overwrites the first. Reading logical key "notes." then returns the other attachment's bytes. The same collapse is reachable through the leaf filename: raw input "report.txt|" is Trim()'d first (line 62), then '|' is stripped, leaving "report.txt" — but "report.|" leaves "report.", which Windows opens as "report". The class doc at lines 10-11 explicitly claims the stripped set keeps a store readable on a Windows host.
verifier_reason: Every link re-derived. `candidate = candidate.TrimStart('.');` is SessionAttachmentPathSanitizer.cs:99 and `sanitized = candidate;` is :128 — no TrimEnd anywhere in the class, and no test pins trailing-dot behaviour (SessionAttachmentPathSanitizerTests.cs:111 pins only leading dots). The output is used verbatim as a directory segment at SessionAttachmentStore.cs:2628 `Path.Combine(ownerSegment, logicalKey, "v" + version..., originalFileName)`, then ResolveUnderRoot:2603 calls `Path.GetFullPath`, which on Windows applies documented normalization ("If a segment ends in a single period, that period is removed"), collapsing keys "notes." and "notes" to one physical directory. The overwrite is real: EncryptedBlobStore.cs:1082 is `File.Move(_tempPath, _destinationPath, overwrite: true)`. I searched for a downstream trim as instructed — the only TrimEnd-family calls under Infrastructure/Data are `Path.TrimEndingDirectorySeparator` (SessionAttachmentStore.cs:2723/2725, DataRetentionService.cs:7425), which do not touch trailing dots. The class doc at lines 10-11 ("The stripped set is identical on every platform so a store written on macOS or Linux stays readable on a Windows host") is therefore false in production today.
verifier_worse: Yes, in two ways. (1) The finder says the read "returns the other attachment's bytes" — that is only the same-length case. OpenReadAsync (SessionAttachmentStore.cs:1375-1415) checks nothing but `decrypted.Length != record.ByteLength`, and IEncryptedBlobStore.OpenReadAsync (IEncryptedBlobStore.cs:63) takes no expected-AAD argument, so a length match silently returns the wrong attachment's plaintext (cross-attachment disclosure within the session) and a length mismatch throws InvalidDataException. Either way the first attachment's ciphertext is already destroyed. (2) The finder missed the portability half the class doc actually promises: a store written on macOS with logical key "notes." creates a real `notes.` directory, which on Windows resolves to `notes` — so the record's RelativePath points at nothing (or at another key's directory), and the store is not readable on the Windows host the doc guarantees. Windows-only, but Windows is a shipped surface (docs/Compendium.README.md:18, `compendium-win-x64`), and this is not any of the listed known issues.

summary: The MCP ambient-session binding TTL is measured against DateTime.UtcNow, a wall clock, so a forward clock step or a suspend/resume longer than the 10-minute TTL expires a live in-flight binding and a backward step keeps expired ones alive.
failure_scenario: BindRequest stamps a binding with `_utcTicksNow()` (line 100) and SweepExpired/IsExpired compare `now - CreatedUtcTicks > _bindingTtl.Ticks` (lines 221, 242). A host that suspends (laptop sleep, VM pause) or takes an NTP step forward of more than DefaultBindingTtl (10 min, line 28) between the send-side bind and the server-side resolve sees the binding gone. ResolveAmbientSessionForToolsCall (ArcanumInternalToolServer.cs:1258-1276) then returns null, and attach_session_file cannot resolve the session it was invoked for — the tool fails with no indication that a clock, not the request, is at fault. A backward step leaves entries un-swept for the duration of the jump plus the TTL.
verifier_reason: Code as cited: SessionAttachmentToolAmbient.cs:40 `_utcTicksNow = static () => DateTime.UtcNow.Ticks`, stamped at :100, compared at :241 (finder said :242) and :221-231 in SweepExpired. Wall-clock TTL is real. But the window is far narrower than the finder implies: the binding is created at ChannelClientTransport.cs:104 immediately before a `_toServer.WriteAsync` on an in-memory channel (ChannelClientTransport.cs:12-18 documents the transport as in-process to ArcanumInternalToolServer with no subprocess or network hop), and resolved at ArcanumInternalToolServer.cs:1258 microseconds later — so a >10-minute forward step or process suspend must land inside that window. Constructible (a laptop suspended mid-tool-call resumes with UtcNow an hour ahead, TryResolveRequest returns null, attach_session_file fails with no hint the clock is at fault), but I cannot bound its frequency. The backward-step half is effectively dead: bindings are removed unconditionally in ArcanumInternalToolServer.cs:1233's `finally`, so un-swept entries do not persist.
